statement: Define vals(T) as the set of node values of T. Define pre(T) as the preorder traversal of T: pre(Null) = [], and pre(Node(v,L,R)) = [v] followed by pre(L) followed by pre(R). For S subseteq vals(root), define flip(T,S) as the tree obtained from T by swapping the left and right children at exactly those nodes whose values belong to S. A swap at a node with fewer than two children does not change the preorder traversal. Whenever the function returns Ok r: (1) if there exists S subseteq vals(root) with pre(flip(root,S)) = voyage, let m = min { |S| : S subseteq vals(root) and pre(flip(root,S)) = voyage }; then r is a list whose entries are exactly the elements of some S_min subseteq vals(root) for which pre(flip(root,S_min)) = voyage and |S_min| = m, in any order, with no repeated entries; (2) if no such S exists, then r = [-1].
preconditions: Let n = len(voyage). root has exactly n nodes, n >= 1 and n <= 100; every node value and every voyage entry lies in {1,...,n}; all node values are distinct; all voyage entries are distinct (hence voyage is a permutation of the node values).
